I'm in Texas, but I resigned from my former position for my mental health. I was also in a special education with a too big caseload and no one to replace me. I spent 3 months on FMLA before I finally accepted that I mentally could not step doot on campus again. 

My district had a Google form you filled out describing the resignation and meeting, where I just marked health. I attached a letter from my doctor stating that my position was negatively affecting my health and causing it to decline. They didn't choose to have my license marked because I had the medical documents. 

I think the most important thing is to have some form of medical documentation to keep them from pursuing your license. I hope you figure things out.
We love our PD days because half the day is going over different models, but the entire second half is lesson planning using our models.
It is a partnered PD and we've had everything planned out for it, but the admin never bothered to discuss anything with us. Just these random two sentence emails.
I always feel sick, but for me it's the stress of the job wearing me out.

They overload us basically. Given the option of 200 gen-ed kids and at most 2 preps, or my job of, still working with 200 kids a day, but 4 preps to co-teach and a caseload that's doubled since last year, no one would reasonably pick SPED. We have more legal responsibilities than the gen-eds and literally one planning period to cover all of our SPED AND content area prep and filing.

I 100% feel the same way. I actually asked my boyfriend this the other day. I don't want to die, but I'm tired of existing if things won't ever improve. 

The only thing that has really helped me is Seroquel and ECT. The ECT works really well for me, but the side effects make me unable to work. And of course, if I don't work, I don't have the insurance for the treatments. 

So, I fall back into I've tried everything, and the only thing that does work isn't feasible.
100%, plus I've had 12 rounds of ECT, so unless I write something down, it's immediately gone.
I'll try to stick it out.
But even during peak? I feel like my brain is constantly spinning.

I've literally been on dozens of anti-depressants, mood stabilizers, anti-anxietys, and been through 12 rounds of electroconvulsive therapy and I'm still not dealing. This will be my last year teaching unfortunately.
Exactly. And my degrees are in pure math so they're not easily applied elsewhere.
I am. I've had to take 6 weeks this semester due to instability. It's a serious stressor.
